The interview then asked eight questions one at a time, each with a stated default, and the reflect-back was confirmed. Six rulings and two amendments became D-42sbt2 and D-e3zm2j.

observation: Q4 proposed redesigning the first-run screen as one edit_user form. The founder answered "why change the welcome screen? Stay focused", so the screen stayed as it was and only its calls changed. The pull came back one level down: architecture revision 1 still dropped the team agent and the inspect-path folder detail, and critique 1 B1 caught that against D-c7jgxy. The plan had not said whether a screen whose backend changes also gets redesigned.

The founder answered "no follow-up after BC7; after BC7 we must be done", and all four families came into this item. observation: The plan said nothing about which task edits the converted retro should act on. The architecture’s F2(b) default guarded only on "the task moved to done". observation: The plan also said nothing about the agent-health crash notices, which were the only live writer to the inbox people see. Architecture revision 1 deleted them without a ruling. Critique 1 B4 flagged that as an unapproved cut, revision 2 put it to the founder as F1 with a default (a health note through edit_user), and the founder accepted it. A cut feature had nearly shipped because the census counted it as part of the notification queue.
evidence: critique-1.md B4(a); architecture.md §0 F1; D-kdqrss

observation: Two critique rounds found 4 and then 1 blockers, and every one was real and would otherwise have been built. B1: the welcome screen lost its team agent and folder detail. B2: edit_user could not create an agent with an identity or agentCategory, and edit_document refuses an agent parent from the UI. B3: reach checked through open_document bumps readCount, which skews search ranking; reach moved to search_*({ids}) and T7a asserts readCount stays unchanged. B4: health notices and the team org-edge kind were cut without a ruling. B5: an agent added in Settings with a blank prompt could never get an identity document. The non-blocking list also produced the needs chain (N4) and the T7a/T7b split (N8).
evidence: critique-1.md, critique-2.md; architecture.md revision 2

observation: In architecture §7 the welcome screen sends folders.add on the create call. No block’s red test covered the server side of that. T5’s red list covers create with run config, identity and subscriptions but not folders, and T10’s SetupFlow test mocks call(). Nobody owned the create-with-folder path, and review 1 found it silently dropped (B1).
evidence: architecture.md §7 step 1, §11 T5 and T10 red tests; review-1.md B1

observation: The architecture did not anticipate the governance crossing rules in four places. Routine could not statically import the moved cron, so the builder injected it as a port (D-fdccrk). @hyperidle/user could not import api-contract or harness-capability, so it hand-mirrors the port shapes (D-72d8sk). The reach doors are hand-typed mirrors (D-nkkjre). connections.add rebuilds its schema locally (D-75a7ba). Each workaround was found by a builder when governance-lint went red. The hand-mirrored and declared shapes are the same family as the later Settings crash.
evidence: D-fdccrk, D-72d8sk, D-nkkjre, D-75a7ba; T-zjmxwe feedback

observation: This is the second item in a row where builders put pipeline ids in comments and test titles. This time the preamble named comments, tests and commit messages explicitly and allowed ids only inside @lore that states the constraint in words. Review 1 still counted 70 added non-@lore lines in 46 files, 29 of them in 18 production files. The T17 sweep used a builder-widened regex and still missed 7 lines (bare "T4"/"T7a" and "architecture.md §"). The reviewer’s idscan.py found them, and a second pass fixed them. The two reviewers disagreed on whether "BC5 T<n>" in describe titles was a violation; the planner settled it by the founder’s rule: added lines only. The sweep regex also false-matched "D-invariants" (D-54kqac). A follow-through then reopened T22 because its @lore told the T19/T22 history.

observation: Two reviewers with separate lenses found four blocking regressions, none overlapping. All passed check, lint, knip and deps (all 0), 77 targeted tests and the seam test. They were: the welcome screen’s folder dropped on create; the team check lost on folder give (so any agent could be given another team’s folder); the profile’s harness banner hardcoded; and every subscription wake forced to DM the install’s oldest person. Each was behaviour main had that the branch lost silently, with no test covering it.
evidence: review-1.md B1, B2; review-2.md; review-1b.md B4

observation: T15’s fix for not_returned forced send_message as the return for every subscription session, and the live harness passed 4/4 lanes. The lanes asserted outcome=completed and the edited document, not that no message was sent. With no thread, send_message goes to soleHumanForAgent, the oldest human in the team or install. So every task edit anywhere made the no-team librarian DM that person, and the retro’s "stop" became impossible. reviewer/opus found this by reading compose.ts, and the desktop walk confirmed it live (Acme Builder DM’d the founder). T20 replaced the forced message with return_status (D-h6sfpa supersedes D-t64zbp). That needed a required-only case in harness-protocol’s return predicate, outside the task’s scope (D-4kr6aw), and the lane now asserts no message row.
evidence: review-1b.md B4; desktop walk 1 note on T-xegkgw; D-t64zbp, D-h6sfpa, D-4kr6aw; T-ffwmfq feedback; commits 30241fbdf, bafd17e05, 02bc14617

observation: reviewer/sonnet re-verified T18 and T19 by reverting the one-line fix in a scratch copy, watching the new test fail with the originally reported error, and restoring the file (git status clean). It also swept every other UserView sub-schema against its port type for the same class of drift and found none. reviewer/opus’s 1b re-verify of B1/B2 was "red by reasoning, not by revert", because builders were still working in the shared worktree.

observation: The four-lane live harness found opencode and cursor-agent ending not_returned on a subscription wake. T14 recorded this as a decision ("reported as observed, not papered over") rather than skipping the lanes. T15 found a two-part cause. First, requiredReturnActions was never set for a subscription wake. Second, the real wake path builds its prompt in assembleSubscriptionPrompt, not in the task-free fallback its first pass fixed, and that composer never told the agent up front how to return. cursor-agent, which has no reactive enforcement, passed on the up-front prompt line alone.
evidence: D-8zsrg9 (superseded), D-t64zbp; T-py3mfd, T-rqt7sj feedback; harness-*.log

On the previous item’s demo database, 0088-0090 then ran clean on real data: humans got a team from the edge, and the librarian’s three routines became paused subscriptions with prompt documents.
evidence: user-subscription-seam.integration.test.ts (commit 60afa11c9); T-6442fw, T-pbk2eg feedback; desktop walk 1 note

observation: Settings crashed to the error boundary only in the packaged app with a real database. UserView.connections.inherited was declared as InheritedReachViewSchema (name/kind/source/health), but the port returns ConnectionView rows, and buildUserView casts "as UserView" without validating. T10 built SettingsConnections from the declared shape (D-q3njmc), and its component tests used fixtures of that shape, so everything was green. T19 read the real fields as a workaround, and T22 fixed the declared schema with a safeParse test against a real-shaped row. T1’s builder had flagged its mirrored views as "best-effort mirrors, not yet proven against a real DB row".
evidence: desktop walk 1 note; review-2b.md 2c; D-q3njmc, D-tm9nrn; T-tj4hmp, T-jv6z5e feedback; T-5qxnk3 feedback
